newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Top hard to call in ballistic dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Top hard to call in ballistic dlr/yen.

text.p: The steepness of dollar/yen's ascent in recent weeks makes top-picking a risky proposition though the dollar managed to brush a long-term resistance level on Wednesday, technical analysts said.
Retracements as dollar/yen advanced became progressively shallower, producing a supporting trendline which rounds upwards into a vertical aspect, they said.

"It's getting parabolic. The corrections are getting very, very muted," said Thom Worden, global technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "Dollar/yen is going to get vertical, unless it takes out the curving trendline."
On Wednesday, the dollar posted a four-year high at 122.78 yen, nearly intersecting a bear-channel resistance line in the 122.80- to 123-yen area, dating back to 1989.

Usually, such long-term technical resistance provide a tempting target to sell into, especially with medium- and long-term technical indicators as deeply overbought as they currently are for the dollar.
But, with dollar/yen on such a steep trajectory, analysts said it is best to wait for a sharp downward move to confirm any kind of top.

"Trying to pick a top exactly is ludicrous in this kind of market," said David Solin, partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. "You are better off ... just waiting until something a little bit more solid develops."
A move through Wednesday's high should prompt a straight line rally to the 124.50/125 yen area, analyst said.
The key short-term trigger for a reversal lies on the curving trendline at 120.90/00 yen, below which technicians said they will feel more comfortable predicting a correction.
In dollar/mark, the retracement from Tuesday's 31-month high at 1.6570 met and slightly overshot a key support objective at 1.6350 before bouncing back on Wednesday.

"If we lose (1.6350 marks) again, then I think we have some risk to the downside at 1.6250," Worden said. "But while it's above there, we're still in an uptrend and the uptrend hasn't been broken yet."
At 1515 EST on Wednesday, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.6421/26, up from 1.6395/00 at the U.S. open. Dollar/yen was at 122.06/11, up from 121.55/65.
